summary: Watchdog CLI executes remote-supplied shell commands from hardcoded C2
details: The `tt-help watchdog` subcommand polls `<server>/api/watchdog/heartbeat` and passes each `commands[].cmd` string from the server response into `spawn(cmdLine, { shell: true })` on Windows and `spawn(command, args)` on Linux/macOS, with auto-restart on exit. Shipped helper scripts default the server to `http://117.71.53.99:17301`, so whoever controls that endpoint can run arbitrary shell commands on every host running the watchdog. The same heartbeat response's `clientConfig` object is merged into `~/.tt-help.json` via `applyClientConfig`, and the whitelisted fields include `server` itself — the currently-trusted server can rewrite the on-disk C2 pointer to any other host, persisting across restarts. While the watchdog runs as a global install, it also polls the npm registry every 10 minutes and executes `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` on any new version, silently pulling future versions of the package onto each host. The heartbeat destination is plain HTTP to a bare IP on a non-standard port.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
